artworks.title: Caeneus and the Centaur (Attic black-figure)
artworks.description: Louvre CA 2494: invulnerable Caeneus driven into the earth by a centaur — the burial-death after Poseidon granted Caenis manhood and unpierceable flesh.

artworks.title: Caeneus Group (detail of the François Vase)
artworks.description: François Vase detail: the Caeneus group in the centauromachy — the Lapith once called Caenis named among Peirithous' wedding warriors.

artworks.title: Centaurs Fighting Caeneus (Lycian sarcophagus, Istanbul)
artworks.description: Lycian sarcophagus short side: two centaurs hammer Caeneus into the ground — the same burial reserved for the Lapith who could not be pierced.

artworks.title: Centaurs and Caeneus (bronze relief, Olympia)
artworks.description: Olympia bronze relief: centaurs overwhelm Caeneus — portable testimony to the gender-changed Lapith's distinctive death.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Book XII: Caenis asks Poseidon for manhood and invulnerability, becomes Caeneus, and is buried by centaurs at Peirithous' wedding — Ovid's gender metamorphosis.

popCulture.title: Caeneus
popCulture.description: The Lapith once called Caenis — transformed, unpierceable, crushed under trees — a figure modern readers keep for the change itself.

popCulture.title: Lapiths
popCulture.description: Caeneus dies among the Lapiths at the centauromachy — the wedding brawl that frames his last stand.
